column1: tags: meta, build, bridge, drawbridge, transform, defense

description: A #meta blueprint that stamps one directional #build four times with transform() so each copy faces a different cardinal direction. The referenced /gate is a 3x3 raising drawbridge whose gw tokens raise the span to the north. transform(rotcw) rotates a referenced blueprint clockwise
column2: and because it is a #build the direction-sensitive machinery rotates with it: that copy raises to the EAST
column3: not the north. transform(rotcw rotcw) is two clockwise turns
column5: and transform(rotccw) turns counter-clockwise to raise WEST. The footprint is a square 3x3
column6: so rotation leaves the shape unchanged and isolates the effect on the raise direction. Each reference also carries a shift() to slide the copy six tiles east of the previous one (three tiles of bridge plus a three tile gap)
column7: so the four gates sit in a row without overlapping. When both markers are on one reference the shift is applied AFTER the transform
column8: so its numbers are read in the final
column9: rotated orientation. Transforms in one call are applied in order and are space separated (rotcw rotcw)
column11: so a CSV cell does not split them. This is the corpus's first transform() example: where meta-tiled-quarters.csv uses shift() to move copies across one floor and meta-residential-tower.csv uses repeat(down 5) to stack them down the Z-axis
column12: transform() rotates and flips them. The sibling transforms are fliph and flipv
column13: which mirror a blueprint left-right or up-down. Build a lever within reach of each bridge and link it after building.
